DOCUMENTS TRANSMITTED TODAY
Plaintiff transmits today, to all counsel of record, the following documents: (1) Plaintiff's
Rule 26(f)(2) Written Proposal and Proposed Discovery Plan Directed to Defendant Meta
Platforms, Inc.; (2) the same, Directed to Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited
Children; (3) the same, Directed to Defendant Katie Hall, Individually; and (4) this common
agenda. Each proposal is complete in itself and seeks the position of the Defendant to which it is
1

directed. Each counsel receives all three proposals so that every appearing party can participate
on common matters.
Each proposal states, in its Section I, what the document is and is not: an opening
proposal under Rule 26(f)(1)-(3), not a discovery request, not a certification of completion, and
not a representation that discovery has commenced. Each proposal states, in its Section II, the
procedural posture and the matters Plaintiff preserves, including the pending motions and
applications and the statement in ECF 84 concerning when discovery begins. Nothing in this
agenda enlarges or narrows those statements.
PARTICIPANTS AND FORMAT
The appearing parties are Plaintiff; Meta Platforms, Inc., through Jesse Beringer and
Hillary Dang of Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP; the National Center for Missing &
Exploited Children, through Padraic K. Keane of Jordan Coyne LLP; and Katie Hall,
individually, through Mr. Keane. The Doe Defendants have not been identified or served and are
not participants. Rule 26(f)(2) makes the attorneys of record and all unrepresented parties that
have appeared jointly responsible for arranging the conference, for attempting in good faith to
agree on the proposed discovery plan, and for submitting the written report.
The conference proceeds by written exchange unless a Defendant objects to that format
in its response and proposes a specific alternative (date, time, and method). No order requiring
attendance in person has been entered. Where a Defendant requests a call limited to remaining
issues after the first exchange, Plaintiff will arrange one; a call, if held, will be confirmed in
writing afterward so that the record of positions remains written.

V.
RECONCILIATION RULES
(1)
(2)
(3)
(4)
Each Defendant's position is attributed to that Defendant only, except where
counsel states expressly that NCMEC and Hall adopt a position jointly.
The report records agreements as agreements and disagreements as separately
stated positions. Joint submission does not require any party to state that a
proposal is agreed when it is not.
A position on a common matter (format, disclosures timing, ESI formats,
privilege method and timing, protective-order procedures, schedule intervals) is
reconciled across all parties. A position on a Defendant-specific matter (subjects,
preservation categories, custodians) is recorded as to that Defendant.
A party that declines to address a subject is recorded as having declined. A party
that does not respond is recorded as not having participated. Neither is recorded as
agreement.
4

(5)
A party may revise a position before the report is submitted by stating the revision
in writing; the report reflects the position as last stated.
VI. TRANSMITTAL NOTE (TEXT OF THE COVERING ELECTRONIC MAIL)
Counsel: Attached are Plaintiff's Rule 26(f)(2) written proposals directed to Meta Platforms,
Inc., to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, and to Katie Hall, individually,
together with a common agenda. Each proposal opens the Rule 26(f) planning conference as to
the Defendant to which it is directed; each counsel receives all three so that every appearing
party can participate on common matters. The proposals are not discovery requests and do not
represent that discovery has commenced; Section II of each states the procedural posture and the
matters Plaintiff preserves, including as to ECF 84. Plaintiff requests each Defendant's written
response, section by section, by October 30, 2026. NCMEC and Hall may respond jointly where
counsel states that both adopt the response. If any Defendant objects to proceeding in writing,
please state the objection and propose a specific alternative. Paper copies follow by first-class
mail. Transmission by electronic mail is for convenience in conferral and is not consent to
service by electronic means under Rule 5(b)(2)(E). — Marvelle J. Ballentine, Plaintiff, pro se.
